translationRepairs: In 721, the ninth year of Kaiyuan, the Shuofang Army military commissioner was established, commanding the Chanyu Grand Protectorate, six prefectures (Xia, Salt, Sui, Yin, Feng, and Sheng), the Dingyuan and Feng'an garrisons, and the eastern, central, and western Accept-the-Surrender fortresses.

In 721, the ninth year of Kaiyuan, the Shuofang Army military commissioner was established, commanding the Chanyu Grand Protectorate, six prefectures (Xia, Yan, Sui, Yin, Feng, and Sheng), the Dingyuan and Feng'an garrisons, and the eastern, central, and western Accept-the-Surrender fortresses.
鹽州 is the prefecture Yan, not the common noun salt; the original list invents “Salt” among named prefectures.
In 728, the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, the Dada Hun Protectorate was abolished.
In 728, the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, the Dahun Protectorate was abolished.
達渾都督府 is the two-character name Dahun; “Dada Hun” splits 達渾 into a false Dada ethnonym plus Hun.
728, sixteenth year. The Dada Hun Protectorate was abolished.
728, sixteenth year. The Dahun Protectorate was abolished.
The same 達渾都督府 must be Dahun in the literal as well; “Dada Hun” is not in the Chinese.
The Shanxi West observation commissioner gained the chief defense commissioner in his duties.
The Shaanxi observation commissioner gained the chief defense commissioner in his duties.
陝西 is Shaanxi (west of Shan), not Shanxi (山西). His/its is only office-holder wording; the proposed after still misnames the circuit.

The Eastern Capital Region observation commissioner was reinstated, filled concurrently by the Left Censorate vice censor-in-chief at Luoyang; Ru Prefecture was restored to his command and the Shanxi West defense and observation commissioner was abolished.

The Eastern Capital Region observation commissioner was reinstated, filled concurrently by the vice censor-in-chief of the detached Censorate at the eastern capital; Ru Prefecture was restored to his command and the Shaanxi defense and observation commissioner was abolished.
留臺 is the detached eastern-capital Censorate, not 左臺, and Luoyang is not in this unit; 陝西 is also Shaanxi, not Shanxi, so the proposed after is still wrong on the circuit name.

The Eastern Capital Region observation commissioner was restored; the Left Censorate vice censor-in-chief at the eastern capital held the post concurrently; it again held Ru Prefecture; the Shanxi West defense and observation commissioner was abolished.

The Eastern Capital Region observation commissioner was restored; the vice censor-in-chief of the detached Censorate at the eastern capital held the post concurrently; it again held Ru Prefecture; the Shaanxi defense and observation commissioner was abolished.
留臺 is not the Left Censorate; the proposed after still renders 陝西 as Shanxi West.
Before long, the five prefectures and Jin Prefecture were abolished; he became military commissioner of the Capital Region Shang Prefecture.
Before long, the five prefectures and Jin Prefecture were removed from his charge; the post became military commissioner of the Capital Region Shang Prefecture.
罷五州及金州 drops those jurisdictions from the commission; the prefectures themselves are not abolished, and 為 marks redesignation of the post.
A Shanxi West chief defense commissioner was appointed and soon raised to military commissioner.
A Shaanxi chief defense commissioner was appointed and soon raised to military commissioner.
陝西 is the circuit west of Shan, romanized Shaanxi; Shanxi West reads as 山西.
The Shanxi West chief defense commissioner was established; soon he was promoted to military commissioner.
The Shaanxi chief defense commissioner was established; soon the post was promoted to military commissioner.
陝西 is Shaanxi, and 尋升為節度使 promotes the office just established, not a named incumbent.
The Shanxi West military commissioner was abolished.
The Shaanxi military commissioner was abolished.
廢陝西節度使 names the same Shaanxi circuit, not Shanxi.
The Shanxi West military commissioner was abolished.
The Shaanxi military commissioner was abolished.
The literal must match 陝西 as Shaanxi, not Shanxi West.

In 882, the second year of Zhonghe, the Wei–Bei military commissioner was granted the honorific name Baoda Army circuit, gained Zhai Prefecture, and the Case Army circuit was established at Yan Prefecture.

In 882, the second year of Zhonghe, the Wei–Bei military commissioner was granted the honorific name Baoda Army circuit, gained Zhai Prefecture, and the Baosai Army circuit was established at Yan Prefecture.
保塞軍 is the Baosai Army; “Case Army” is a false rendering of 塞 and is not in the source.
882, second year. The Wei-Bei circuit was granted the honorific name Baoda Army circuit, Zhai Prefecture was added to its jurisdiction, and at Yan Prefecture the Case Army circuit was established.
882, second year. The Wei-Bei circuit was granted the honorific name Baoda Army circuit, Zhai Prefecture was added to its jurisdiction, and at Yan Prefecture the Baosai Army circuit was established.
The literal likewise requires Baosai for 保塞軍, not the invented name Case Army.
The Case Army circuit was renamed the Ningse Army circuit, and later renamed again as the Weiguo Army circuit.
The Baosai Army circuit was renamed the Ningse Army circuit, and later renamed again as the Weiguo Army circuit.
更保塞軍節度 continues the same Baosai Army name; Case is still a false reading of 塞.
The Case Army circuit was renamed the Ningse Army circuit; later it was again renamed the Weiguo Army circuit.
The Baosai Army circuit was renamed the Ningse Army circuit; later it was again renamed the Weiguo Army circuit.
The literal rename line also starts from 保塞軍, which is Baosai, not Case.
